cause: A2 local preference persistence and bound confirmation modules do not exist yet; their contract tests fail at import time.
impact: The product cannot persist default-off local memory preferences or bind an enable/delete action to a one-time user confirmation.
lesson: Create and observe the persistence and confirmation contracts before connecting Settings or mutation routes.

cause: Notebook routes still require browser-supplied domain_memory_use and domain_memory_iteration flags, so local persisted settings cannot control retrieval.
impact: Notebook memory is not yet bound to the server-owned per-project settings contract.
lesson: Remove request-local durable preference inputs before wiring the local runtime into Notebook compilation.

cause: The atomic settings writer assumes os.write writes the whole payload in one call, so a partial write can replace the durable preference document with truncated JSON.
impact: A partial filesystem write can make local memory settings unavailable after a seemingly successful update.
lesson: Durable preference writes must loop until every byte is written before fsync and replace.

cause: The public preference-store constructor checks only its final directory and can follow a symlinked ancestor.
impact: A direct caller could persist local memory settings outside the intended filesystem boundary.
lesson: Every public local-storage constructor must reject symlinked ancestors, not only bootstrap paths.

cause: The read route classifies a corrupt enabled local memory store as a client request error instead of an unavailable server runtime.
impact: Clients receive a misleading 400 response for a fail-closed local memory outage.
lesson: Storage integrity failures must surface as service unavailability, never as malformed client input.

cause: The preference writer now loops until every byte is written before fsync and atomic replacement.

lesson: Every public local-storage entry point needs the same non-symlink ancestry guarantee as bootstrap.
